chunks.content: ## Adding a Pull Chain in CLO This section explains how to add and position a pull chain using CLO’s 3D and 2D tools, covering the pull chain placement, adjustment, and simulation to prevent panel layer penetration. 1. Open your project file in CLO. 2. Select the **3D Pull Tool** from the 3D toolbar. 3. Hover the mouse over the desired position on the garment's edge to add a pull chain. A blue dot will appear indicating a valid insertion point. 4. Click twice to add and complete the pull chain on that side. 5. The pull chain can also be added similarly in the 2D window by clicking at the appropriate positions. 6. Between the two pull chain endpoints, a black box line will display, indicating the boundary for pull chain modeling. 7. Use the left arrow tool to drag the pull head to the correct position before simulation. 8. To prevent the inner panel layer from penetrating during simulation, adjust the pull chain position and set its layer accordingly. 9. After stabilizing the simulation, turn it off and restore the pull chain layer to its original state. 10. Zoom in to inspect the pull chain and verify the pull head orientation. 11. Switch to the texture surface view to check if any side of the pull chain appears gray, which means it is facing the opposite direction. 12. Use the move tool to select and correct the pull chain direction. 13. Re-run simulation to stabilize and close it once the pull chain is properly positioned. 14. You can drag the pull head again with the left arrow tool to adjust the closed position and update the 3D effect. 15. To delete the entire pull chain, select it and click the delete option. --- ## Pull Chain Options and Controls This section covers additional pull chain controls, including direction switching, freezing, display toggling, rotation, and resetting position, with explanations of their functions. - When a pull chain is added, the two sides are initially reversed. Clicking the direction switch button aligns both sides in the same direction. - The pull chain component can be re-activated or frozen to control visibility and editing. - Clicking on the pull head toggles the pull chain display or deletes it entirely. - Surface rotation functions similarly to panel rotation, useful for asymmetrical pull heads to flip left and right. - Pull heads can be moved by specified distances or reset to their original positions. - All additional options mirror those of the pull chain, allowing consistent control over the component. --- ## Modifying Pull Chain Style and Specifications This section explains how to customize pull chain types, styles, and specifications using the Property Editor, including product information and material settings. 1. Select the pull chain in the Object Window. 2. In the Property Editor, view and edit the pull chain name. 3. Enter product details such as product number and supplier information. 4.

chunks.content: - All additional options mirror those of the pull chain, allowing consistent control over the component. --- ## Modifying Pull Chain Style and Specifications This section explains how to customize pull chain types, styles, and specifications using the Property Editor, including product information and material settings. 1. Select the pull chain in the Object Window. 2. In the Property Editor, view and edit the pull chain name. 3. Enter product details such as product number and supplier information. 4. Set the pull chain as **single** or **double**; if double, select the pull head direction (either double or double-sided). 5. Click the triangle beside the type option to select the pull chain type: - Vertical pull chain - Metal pull chain - Nylon pull chain - Invisible pull chain 6. Choose the pull chain component type: pull ruler, pull head, or pull piece. 7. Customize index types such as open or closed tail and set upper and lower part types. 8. Adjust specifications including width, weight, and thickness. 9. Start editing the material pattern of the pull chain components. --- ## Editing Pull Chain Length and Simulation This section details how to adjust the pull chain length and simulate its open and close states. - In the 3D window, select the Move Tool and click on the pull chain length. - Use the Property Editor to check and edit the pull chain length. - Open or close the pull chain by simulating the chain’s movement. - Use Ctrl + Z to undo changes and restore the original state. - The pull chain can be maintained in an open state if desired. - Choose the pull chain opening direction and specify which side the pull head is on. - Adjust particle diameter to control the spacing between pull chain particles. - Use the folding option to adjust folding strength and angle between the pull chain and the garment panel. --- ## Material Customization for Pull Chain Components This section explains how to assign and customize materials for different pull chain parts, including metal presets and fabric color matching. - Materials are divided into pull ruler and pull band, which can be edited separately. - Select the pull ruler type as metal and choose a metal preset such as gold. - Adjust the gold color to closely match the fabric color. - For fabric components, set the color to match the garment fabric. - Pull heads, pull pieces, and finger components can be selected and modified together or individually. - Use the Move Tool to select individual components for separate size and material adjustments. - Modify material properties in the Property Editor to match the desired metal or fabric finish. --- ## Saving and Applying Pull Chain Presets This section covers how to save customized pull chains as reusable presets and how to apply them in CLO projects. - After completing the pull chain customization, select the pull chain in the Object Window.
